paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. An oath the Israelites took doesn't expire when the people who made it are gone (2 Samuel 21:2). Saul tried to kill the Gibeonites, and the LORD said the famine was "because of the blood shed by Saul and his family" (2 Samuel 21:1). I think that should make every one of us slow down before we say "I promise."

Now look at what David does: he sought the face of the LORD first (2 Samuel 21:1). Then he summoned the Gibeonites and asked, "What shall I do for you?" (2 Samuel 21:3). He asked THEM, friend, and that's a whole lesson on making a wrong right. This one is heavy, and I think the pain in it is real, so I won't dress it up.

Then the story ends with something quiet. Rizpah kept her watch on a rock, and David gathered the bones of Saul and Jonathan along with the bones of the seven (2 Samuel 21:10, 13). The passage says, "After they had done everything the king had commanded, God answered their prayers for the land" (2 Samuel 21:14). So when you find out you owe somebody, seek the LORD, listen to the one who was hurt, and make it right, because I've sat in a dark drawer long enough to know that things left alone just collect dust.
